title: month-boundary-burst-carveout-for-reserved-accounts
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a safe carryover policy and engineering flow for reserved-capacity customers who create short mid-month bursts that cross a month boundary (e.g., usage spikes that begin in month N and complete in month N+1). The goal is to avoid double-billing, avoid unexpected hard rejections at boundary windows, and preserve predictable reserved throughput while keeping accounting accurate for monthly commitments.
background: We have recurring incidents and customer support tickets when long-running inference batches or streaming sessions start in the last hour of the billing month and continue into the next month. Current behavior: token usage is attributed to the request start month and the request end month in different subsystems, which causes inconsistent quota enforcement (some requests get allowed by reserved burst capacity in month N but are rejected in month N+1) and creates confusing invoice adjustments. This is most common for reserved capacity customers using persistent streaming sessions, long generation requests, and tenant migrations between dedicated pools.
proposed_solution: Introduce a month-boundary carryover window and a burst-carveout accounting path: (1) Associate each request with a single canonical quota month using a deterministic tie-breaker (prefer request start timestamp if request start and end cross months, with optional tenant override for legal/regulatory needs). (2) Implement a transient 'boundary-burst-carveout' token reservation that reserves capacity from month N for requests that begin within a configurable grace window before a month boundary (default 30 minutes). (3) On month transition, automatically reconcile carved tokens; if the carved tokens exceed a customer's committed monthly allocation, create a queued correction job that: a) applies prorated charge adjustments, b) emits an audit event, and c) flags for manual review if delta > threshold. (4) Ensure all authoritative systems (quota enforcer, billing, usage-exports) consume the canonical month label for a request rather than local epoch rounding. (5) Provide an admin-facing flag to disable carryover for tenants that require strict per-calendar billing.
acceptance_criteria: Requests that start before month boundary within grace window continue uninterrupted after boundary without rejection due to month switch
Usage is attributed consistently across quota enforcer, billing pipeline, and usage reporting (end-to-end tests show same month label)
No silent double-billing: any cross-month correction is either automatic and within policy or surfaced as an invoice adjustment event
Feature toggle exists per-tenant and defaults to ON for reserved-capacity customers
Audit events emitted for every carryover decision with request id, tenant id, start_ts, end_ts, canonical_month
implementation_steps: Schema change: add canonical_month (YYYY-MM) string to request meta and usage export schema
Quota enforcer: read canonical_month and use it for quota checks; implement boundary-burst-carveout reservation path
Billing pipeline: prefer canonical_month when grouping tokens into month buckets; implement correction job to handle over-allocations
Edge cases: add tenant opt-out flag and honor it in enforcer and billing
Backfill: write reconciliation job for last 3 months to find mismatches between old behavior and new canonical_month labeling
QA: add integration tests for streaming sessions, long-gen requests, and simulated DST and timezone transitions
Docs: update billing FAQ and Console reserved capacity docs to describe behavior and admin controls
Telemetry: add metrics for carveout_reservations, corrections_queued, corrections_manual_review_count
test_plan: Unit tests: canonical_month assignment logic for start_ts/end_ts permutations
Integration tests: end-to-end generated workload where long-generation spans boundary; verify no rejection and single-month attribution
Chaos test: simulate month rollover at high QPS and verify enforcer handles reservations without latency spikes
Simulated migration: tenant move between reserved pools during grace window and verify borrowing semantics
Regression test: run existing billing export compare job to ensure export parity for unaffected tenants
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert if carveout_reservations > 2% of reserved_capacity for a tenant sustained > 1h
Alert if reconciliations queue length grows > 5000 jobs
Dashboards: monthly carryover volume, correction dollar impact, number of manual reviews
SLO: quota-enforcer 99.9p latencies must not regress when carveout path enabled
rollout_plan: Feature toggle behind tenant flag in control plane; enable for internal test tenants first
Smoke test with 3 pilot customers (one PLG, two reserved enterprise) during off-peak month boundary
Monitor for 72h after pilot; promote to gradual rollout across all reserved customers over 2 weeks
After full rollout, run backfill reconciliation for previous 3 months and surface any billing adjustments to finance team
rollback_plan: Flip tenant-level toggle off (fast path) to stop using canonical_month for new requests
If rollback required after rollout, queue reconciliation to revert any in-flight carveout reservations and create temporary invoice hold for affected customers
Postmortem and manual crediting flow if automated adjustments exceeded thresholds
